questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses and the content within them and especially the specialization with conservation science. The destination also opened up opportunities for get in contact with researchers with interest in biodiversity and ecosystem function.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university was very helpful with VISA and everything relating to this upon arrival. However, lecture content and timetable information was received late and therefor hard to plan and prepare for traveling abroad.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A welcome week was planned together with other master students within the same field, which have been beneficial to discuss and get new perspectives across different master programs.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There are many different webpages to search for housing, I used varcityliving which have been fair and helpful.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The rental contracts are fixed within the dates you sign for. It is not possible to end the contract unless you find someone to take over your rental.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Started with contact to the administration and the SUFONAMA contact person (which also becomes your personal tutor). Descriptions are available and the university webpage was intuitive to fill out personal detail with contact information and picture upload to prepare for the university keycard. 
Several documents have to be signed and filled out but overall good guidance to make all these different steps possible to get through.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Guidance for both registration and VISA process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There were no choice to choose between different course. It would have been nice if there were more flexibility to choose different courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Follow the instruction and do not be afraid the contact the university, they will be very helpful over the phone to and guide you through the process.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was well, suitable and challenged to get better understanding of academic writing. All courses had essays, reports or other written assessment related to the course content and learning objectives. The written examination assessments could have been combined with an oral assessment.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more lecture based and a lot of papers to read and self studying was more apart of the teaching style compared to UCPH where it was more field based and in class discussion.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
* Conservation Science
* Agriculture & Environment

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
*Research Planning & Communication	
*Thesis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Conservation Science was academic and informative with lots of feedback on assignments to improve writing. The thesis process gives opportunities to work with your own project within the field and many professor are very willing to here about ideas and possible projects.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The visa application and health insurance were expansive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is affordable but public transport were more expensive than expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have many different societies you can join and it is free

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts of societies with sports like badminton, salling, cake baking, water sports and discussion clubs within different fields of interest, for example zoology.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Make use of the national park for many beautiful walks and hikes with fellow students. The sea and many different lakes are also nearby to enjoy both sports and social activities like bonfire at the beach.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the nature and surroundings that bangor and Wales have to offer. Good to explore and recharge batteries for the next intense periods of studying.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The societies are very open for people to join, so it was easy to get know new people also from other programs. The british english took a bit time to get use to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join your fellow students at pubs and different non-alcoholic activities or do not be afraid to suggest a walk nearby or hike in Snowdonia.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: To understand the british english. A lot of new word especially if the locals use slang.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The casual and relaxed pub culture, it's possible to also drink a cup of tea at the pub.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The beautiful location and opportunities to enjoy nature and go for long walks in the mountains. 
Researchers and professors are very approachable, helpful and interested in the students. 
Free societies and sports to join with fellow students across fields.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university old library is silents and good for studying. One of the more open space areas for studying are open 24/7 for students with a keycard.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know other students with different backgrounds and nationalities which expanded my network and allowed for so many good debates and discussion within sustainable forest and nature management. And the university is open for you to join other course even though you are not doing the assessments and just listening in on a topic that have special interest for you.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Academic essay writing

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
